terms.comment: Someone’s arrival or stepping in; also of things that come between (interventū noctis, Caes. BG 3.15).

terms.gloss: intervene, step in between; of a tribune, veto
evidence: Cic. Leg. 3.8: nisi mihi levissimus tribūnus plēbis intercessisset (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally to come or be between; so to intervene for or against someone, and in Roman politics to veto a measure. The noun is intercessiō (veto; intervention).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 10.27.2: sī tē in istam pācificātiōnem nōn interpōnis (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Q. fr. 3.4.5: mē nihil interpōnō
terms.comment: To put oneself into a matter, for good or ill; mē nihil interpōnō is “I’m staying out of it”.

terms.gloss: come between, come in during, come upon, break in on; intervene
evidence: Caes. BG 6.37: cāsū Germānī equitēs interveniunt (Lewis & Short)
Ter. And. 4.3.17: spōnsae pater intervenit (Lewis & Short)

phrases.english: The brothers are squabbling; I don’t want to get involved.

phrases.latin: saepe audīvī inter ōs atque offam multa intervenīre posse
phrases.english: I have often heard that much can come between the mouth and the morsel

phrases.latin: interveniunt amīcī ex proximīs oppidīs, partemque diēī ad sē trahunt
phrases.english: friends drop in from the nearest towns and take part of the day for themselves

sources: Lewis & Short: intercedo · Lewis & Short: interpono · Lewis & Short: interventus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 181, 334.
